Let x = √(a(a+b+c)/(bc)), y = √(b(a+b+c)/(ca)), z = √(c(a+b+c)/(ab)), all positive reals. Then θ = arctan x + arctan y + arctan z.

Use the identity:
tan(A+B+C) = (x+y+z − xyz) / (1 − xy − yz − zx).

Let S = a+b+c.

- xy = √(ab S² /(c² ab))... compute: xy = √( a·b·S² / (bc·ca) ) = S/c.
- Similarly yz = S/a, zx = S/b.
- xyz = √( abc·S³ / (abc)² ) = √(S³/(abc)).
- x+y+z = √(S/(abc)) · (a+b+c) = S√S/√(abc) (since x = √(a²S/(abc)) = a√S/√(abc)).

So x+y+z = S√S/√(abc) = xyz.

Hence the numerator x+y+z − xyz = 0.

The denominator: 1 − S(1/a+1/b+1/c) = 1 − S(ab+bc+ca)/(abc). Since S(ab+bc+ca) ≥ 9abc > abc, the denominator is nonzero (negative).

Therefore tan θ = 0/(nonzero) = 0.

Check: θ is a multiple of π; indeed each arctan is in (0, π/2) and the denominator is negative with numerator zero, so θ = π.
